chunks: And with this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) — he said:

I asked him about a person in a state of janabah who carries a rakwa (small leather water vessel) or a tawra (basin) and inserts a finger into it. He said: «If his hand was impure (najis), he should pour it out; and if no impurity had touched his hand, he should perform ghusl from it. This is from what Allah the Exalted said:
He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion.» [Q 22:78]»

key_terms.التَّوْرَ: tawra — a wide basin or bowl
key_terms.الرَّكْوَةَ: rakwa — a small leather vessel used to carry water for purification
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: person in a state of janabah — major ritual impurity requiring ghusl before worship
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship, constriction, undue difficulty in religious obligation
key_terms.قَذِرَةً: ritually impure, unclean (najis) — the legal ground for discarding the water

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rule about a person in janabah who inserts a finger into a water vessel: must the water be discarded or can it be used for ghusl?
ai.summary: Abu Basir reports asking Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether a person in a state of janabah who dips a finger into a small water vessel may still use that water for ghusl. The Imam rules that if the hand was ritually impure (najis), the water must be poured out; if the hand was clean, ghusl may be performed from it. The Imam anchors this practical easement in Q 22:78, affirming that Allah has imposed no hardship in the religion.
